clue.text: Seek penetrating opinion of carrier

blocks.note: 'my bet is' means 'my opinion is'; this piece is split open

explanation.surface: Someone trying to find out what a porter or courier thinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A basket is a container for holding and transporting things, so it is a carrier.

clue.text: Party in opposition originally supporting embargo taking in Spain

in a down entry a supporting piece holds the rest up from below, so it comes last

E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
the initial letter of the word

explanation.surface: Politicians in opposition backing a Spanish trade embargo at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A beano is British slang for a lively celebration or spree.
explanation.definitionFit: Beano is informal British slang for a festive party or jolly outing.

clue.text: Very small transmitter left inside

explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slight or meagre, as in slender means or a slender chance, so very small.

clue.text: Law passed to have an effect on workers in hospital department

men as in workmen

explanation.surface: A new statute that will change things for staff in a hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: An enactment is a statute or law that a legislature has passed.

clue.text: Like version Tom abridged

blocks.note: a take is one version or interpretation, as in 'my take on it'
the name with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: Something resembling a shortened edition of a book by someone called Tom.
explanation.definitionFit: To take to someone is to come to like them, so the phrasal verb is a synonym of the verb like.

clue.text: Bring together some of lama's stories

blocks.note: the letters run across the apostrophe and the word break

explanation.surface: Collecting a selection of a Tibetan monk's tales.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate a quantity of things.

clue.text: Nonsense verse eventually seen on tree after tree

indicators.note: eventually means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept
in a down entry, sitting on something means coming above it, so the order runs top to bottom
after places the second tree behind the first in the answer

blocks.note: the final letter of the word
the yew is an evergreen tree
the ash is a deciduous tree

explanation.surface: Bad poetry eventually carved on tree after tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'tree' gives two different trees, read in clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyewash is informal for nonsense or humbug, talk meant to deceive.

clue.text: Implicit qualities observable working with verse regularly

the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: Hidden meanings that show up when you work through poetry steadily.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are subtle implications or suggestions beyond the obvious meaning, so implicit qualities.

clue.text: Allow space to perform with style

blocks.note: to make a speech or a move is to perform it
a way of doing something is a manner or style

explanation.surface: A performer asking for room on stage to show off with panache.
explanation.definitionFit: To make way is to step aside and leave room for someone else to pass.

clue.text: Write about outstanding medium-fast bowlers

indicators.note: about here means around, so the first word is wrapped around the second

blocks.note: to pen is to write; this piece goes outside
ace means outstanding, first-rate
M is the standard abbreviation for medium, as on clothing sizes

explanation.walkthrough: 'medium-fast' looks like one description of the bowlers, but the hyphen splits it: medium gives a letter and only 'fast bowlers' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, pacemen are bowlers who rely on speed rather than spin, so fast bowlers.

clue.text: A useful thing for Rocker's adversary surrounded by civility

indicators.note: surrounded by means enclosed on all sides, so one piece sits inside the other

explanation.walkthrough: Mods (scooters, sharp suits) and rockers (motorbikes, leather) were rival British youth subcultures of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: A commodity, in its older sense, is something useful or valuable, an article of use.

clue.text: Surprisingly into disco admitting new circumstances

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Conditions are the prevailing state of affairs around something, the same as its circumstances.

clue.text: Labour for instance not initially interested in painting and sculpture

explanation.walkthrough: Labour is one of Britain's two main political parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone arty shows an interest in the visual arts, often with a hint of pretension.

clue.text: Rid of power to incite

blocks.note: P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the front: 'Rid of' is the verb sense of the answer, followed by its object in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge a place of something is to cleanse it by getting rid of it.

clue.text: Sick soldiers seen in variegated colours ridiculed publicly

ill means sick
OR, other ranks, are soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Ailing troops in camouflage being mocked in public.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillory someone is to expose them to public ridicule, from the old wooden frame of punishment.

clue.text: No more than short slogan relating to commerce

blocks.note: mere means no more than, as in 'a mere child'; shortened by one letter
a chant is a slogan repeated by a crowd

explanation.surface: Dismissing a catchphrase as being merely about trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, as in merchant navy or merchant bank, the word describes things concerned with trade.

clue.text: Dicky sincere? Go and see

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so the letters are in poor shape and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asking whether Dicky is genuine and suggesting a visit to find out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a man's name, but it is the British slang adjective for unsound, as in a dicky heart.

clue.text: Shared out everything turning to note daughter

blocks.note: all means everything
taken as written, then turned round
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.definitionFit: Allotted means apportioned, given out in shares to each person.

clue.text: Experienced performer of ancient Chinese dance primarily

blocks.note: ancient means old
the Han are the majority ethnic group of China
the initial letter of the word

explanation.definitionFit: An old hand is a veteran, someone highly practised and experienced at a task.

clue.text: Searches finding doctor overwhelmed by expenditure mostly

explanation.definitionFit: To comb a place is to search it thoroughly, so combs works as a synonym of searches.

clue.text: Lacking interest in unnamed butcher

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Mundane means dull and ordinary, so lacking any interest or excitement.

clue.text: Not against change of opponent

indicators.note: a change of something alters its form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A paradox about someone who is not against you yet becomes your opponent.

clue.text: Become apparent with an increase in pay

blocks.note: the indefinite article in its short form

clue.text: Section on largely sophisticated information gatherer

clue.text: Deny knowledge of girl's promise after first of accusations

clue.text: Ruse right for a shirker

clue.text: Failing to change sides

second meaning: to desert to the enemy, a verb
